RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-female panel is not evidence of anything on its own. Panels skew by sector and candidate pool; four women deciding could equally have favoured you. Raising it makes you look like you're reading bias into a demographic snapshot, and it will overshadow your genuinely stronger point.

That point is the qualifications comparison: a master's in educational leadership and five years of actual leadership experience versus unspecified "courses" and classroom experience only. That's a concrete, documentable gap, and it's what a tribunal or ombudsman would examine.

Also pursue the unanswered request — most jurisdictions require written reasons within a set period. Send a formal follow-up citing the relevant rule. Their silence, and their eventual reasoning, will tell you far more than the panel's composition.
